To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
co-operative multicontact plasticity stabilizes synaptic connections and that this plasticity is essential for the rewiring of neocortical circuits in response to peripheral lesions.
multicontact co-operativity stabilizes networks and that multicontact plasticity can account for the rewiring of neocortical circuits in response to sensory experience.
multicontact co-operativity in structural plasticity stabilizes neocortical circuits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of computational models of neural networks in order to understand their information-processing capabilities.
the mechanisms of synaptic structural plasticity and their impact on the dynamics and connectivity of neural circuits.
the question, how a network can learn and maintain stable memories of the environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our plasticity rule is able to explain the multicontact structure of synaptic connections in adult neocortex and that it can account for the observed structural reorganization of cortical networks after lesion.
the multicontact co-operativity of spike-timing– dependent plasticity is essential for the formation of long-term stable synaptic memories.
the multicontact structure of excitatory synapses is a consequence of the interplay between the co-operativity of the multiple synapses and the competition between the multiple presynaptic neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the co-operative nature of synaptic contacts stabilizes the activity of neurons in the adult brain.
multicontact co-operativity is a key feature of spike-timing– dependent structural plasticity in neocortical circuits.

the co-operativity of multiple synaptic contacts in a postsynaptic dendritic spine can be explained by a simple, biologically plausible plasticity rule that stabilizes both the firing rate of the postsynaptic neuron and the correlation between the pre- or postsynaptic activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multicontact co-operativity stabilizes networks.
multicontact co-operativity is a key ingredient of spike-timing– dependent plasticity rules that are compatible with the structural organization of adult neocortices.
the co-operation between synaptic contacts on the same postsynaptic neuron can explain why the adult neocortices are organized by multicontact synapses.
